t: GDP per person and population, year 1 to today (Maddison Project)
src: Bolt & van Zanden, Maddison Project Database 2020, via Our World in Data
about: The standard long-run estimates of how rich every country has been, back to Roman times for some. Values are in 2011 international dollars (adjusted for prices so countries and years compare).
q: When did China fall behind Europe, and when did it start catching up?
How long did it take the US to double its income per person?

t: US stocks since 1871: S&P composite, earnings, dividends, CAPE
src: Robert Shiller’s data, via datasets/s-and-p-500 on GitHub
about: Monthly US stock prices since 1871 with earnings, dividends, inflation, long-term interest rates and Shiller’s cyclically adjusted P/E (CAPE). Recent months may show 0 for figures not yet published.
q: How often has the market lost half its value?
Does a high CAPE predict poor returns over the next 10 years?

t: Gold price since 1833 (monthly, US$ per ounce)
src: datasets/gold-prices on GitHub (World Bank, Bundesbank, Harvard sources)
about: The dollar price of gold. Flat for long stretches under the gold standard, then free-floating after 1971.
q: Why was the gold price flat until 1971?

t: Oil prices: Brent since 1987, WTI since 1986 (monthly)
src: US Energy Information Administration via datasets/oil-prices
about: Monthly Brent crude price. Spikes line up with wars, embargoes and crises.
q: What happened to oil in 1990, 2008, 2014, 2020 and 2022?

t: US 10-year Treasury yield since 1953 (monthly)
